findings.observation: Reviewed existing conditions sheets 8 and 9. Vision check on Sheet 8 found that street ROW labels (Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, Nash Avenue) indicate 'R.O.W. VARIES' but do not provide specific numerical width dimensions. Vision check on Sheet 9 confirmed the same - no numerical ROW width dimensions are shown for existing streets.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires existing ROW widths to be both shown AND dimensioned. While the plans acknowledge ROW exists and note that widths vary, no specific measurements (e.g., '50 feet ROW') are provided. The label 'VARIES' indicates acknowledgment of ROW but does not satisfy the dimensioning requirement. Per GRD-01, existing ROW widths must be numerically dimensioned on the existing conditions or grading sheets.
findings.explanation: Existing ROW widths labeled as 'VARIES' but not numerically dimensioned on existing conditions sheets 8 and 9.
findings.resolution: Add numerical ROW width dimensions for existing right-of-way along Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, Nash Avenue, and South Lamar Boulevard on the existing conditions or grading plan sheets.

findings.observation: Reviewed grading plan Sheet 21. Vision check confirmed the plan shows both existing and proposed behind-the-curb improvements including sidewalks (with proposed variable width public sidewalk easement along Collier Street labeled), ADA paths (shown in legend and on plan with spot elevations), landscape areas (shown with hatching pattern per legend), and existing trees to remain (shown with tree symbols). The plan includes extensive grading details with spot elevations and contours for work between curb and property line.
findings.reasoning: Behind-the-curb improvements include sidewalks, ramps, landscape strips, trees, and work between curb and property line. The grading plan shows these elements spatially and with grading information. While lighting is not shown on the grading plan (typical, as it's usually on a separate electrical plan), the plan adequately shows the physical improvements and grading for sidewalks, ADA paths, landscape areas, and trees. The plan references landscape sheets for additional tree and planting details, which is standard practice.
findings.explanation: Grading plan Sheet 21 shows existing and proposed behind-the-curb improvements including sidewalks, ADA paths, landscape areas, and trees with supporting grading information.

findings.observation: Reviewed grading plan Sheet 21 blocks and guide. The sheet legend clearly defines existing contours (shown as dashed lines labeled with numbers like '535') and proposed contours (shown as solid lines labeled with numbers in parentheses like '(535)'). Vision check confirmed both existing and proposed contours are visible throughout the grading plan, showing the transition from existing to proposed grades.
findings.reasoning: A grading plan with existing and proposed grade lines is required to show how the site will be regraded from current conditions to final conditions. The presence of both line types in the legend and their application throughout the plan demonstrates compliance. The distinction between dashed (existing) and solid parenthetical (proposed) contours allows contractors to understand cut and fill requirements.
findings.explanation: Grading plan Sheet 21 shows both existing contours (dashed lines) and proposed contours (solid lines), meeting the requirement for existing and proposed grade lines.

findings.observation: Reviewed dimensional control and site plan Sheet 14. Per the validation methodology, ROW improvement dimensions can appear anywhere in the plan set, not on a specific sheet. Vision check on Sheet 14 found explicit dimensions for ROW improvements along Collier Street: 8-foot planting zone, 5-foot clear zone, and 5-foot sidewalk. These dimensions define the behind-the-curb improvements within the ROW and public sidewalk easement.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires dimensions for new or modified ROW improvements to be shown somewhere in the plan set. The validation methodology explicitly notes not to require dimensions on a specific sheet, but to check for general presence. Dimensions for sidewalk (5'), clear zone (5'), and planting zone (8') along Collier Street satisfy this requirement by showing the width allocations for ROW improvements. These are the types of dimensions needed for constructability and code compliance verification.
findings.explanation: ROW improvement dimensions shown on Sheet 14 including 8' planting zone, 5' clear zone, and 5' sidewalk along Collier Street frontage.

findings.observation: Reviewed project description from README and facts.md. This is an infill redevelopment project on existing lots with frontages on existing public streets (South Lamar Blvd, Collier Street, Kinney Avenue, Evergreen Avenue). The project proposes ROW dedications and sidewalk improvements but does not involve construction of new public roadways. Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) shows on-site parking, driveways, and site paving, not new public street construction. Vision check confirmed Sheet 13 shows horizontal plan view only for on-site development, not roadway construction plan/profile views. No roadway construction plan and profile sheets found in the plan set.
findings.reasoning: New roadway construction refers to creating new public streets with horizontal and vertical alignment design, requiring plan and profile views showing centerline geometry, grades, cross-sections, and roadway features. This project involves private site development with connections to existing streets. ROW improvements (sidewalks, dedications) are not the same as roadway construction. The absence of dedicated roadway plan/profile sheets and the project description confirm no new roadway construction is proposed.
findings.explanation: No new roadway construction proposed; project involves infill development on existing street frontages with ROW improvements but no new public streets.

findings.observation: Same as CC-23-05. No new roadway construction proposed. Target speed notation is a requirement for new roadway design to establish design parameters for geometry, sight distance, and traffic control devices. This project does not involve new roadway construction.
findings.reasoning: Target speed is required only when new roadways are being constructed. Since no new public roadways are proposed (only on-site driveways and parking, plus ROW improvements to existing streets), the target speed notation requirement does not apply. The condition 'If new roadway construction proposed' is not met.
findings.explanation: No new roadway construction proposed; target speed notation requirement does not apply to this infill development project.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) which shows striping for on-site parking stalls and fire lanes. The condition is 'If new roadway construction or work in ROW'. While there is work in ROW (sidewalks, curbs, ADA ramps), this item specifically addresses 'roadway' signage and striping in ROW per the item text 'for new or modified roadway in ROW'. The ROW work consists of pedestrian improvements (sidewalks, ramps), not roadway modifications. No new or modified roadway lanes, shoulders, or travel surfaces in the public ROW require signage and striping plans.
findings.reasoning: This item targets roadway signage and striping plans for vehicular travel lanes in the ROW, not general site signage. The ROW improvements are pedestrian facilities. The striping shown on Sheet 13 is for private on-site parking and fire lanes, not public roadway striping. Since there is no roadway construction or modification in the ROW that would require roadway pavement markings and signage, this requirement is not triggered.
findings.explanation: No roadway construction or roadway modifications in ROW; ROW work consists of pedestrian improvements (sidewalks, ramps) which do not require roadway signage/striping plans.

findings.observation: Reviewed grading plans (Sheets 21-22) and dimensional control plans (Sheets 14-15). Sheet 21 legend shows 'PROPOSED LOW PROFILE WALLS' but no elevations. Sheet 14 legend shows 'PROPOSED RETAINING WALL WITH GUARDRAIL'. Vision check on Sheet 14 confirmed retaining walls with guardrails are shown along the northern boundary but do NOT include explicit top and bottom elevation labels (such as 'TW' or 'BW'). The presence of guardrails indicates walls likely exceed 2 feet in height (guardrails are safety features typically required for walls over 30-42 inches). Vision check on Sheet 21 found spot elevations and contours on both sides of walls but no labeled top/bottom wall elevations.
findings.reasoning: The condition 'If retaining walls >2 feet proposed' appears to be met given the guardrail presence. While spot elevations exist nearby that could theoretically be used to calculate wall height, the checklist item specifically requires 'top and bottom elevations' to be shown. This typically means explicit elevation labels on the walls themselves (e.g., 'TOP OF WALL = 545.00, BOT OF WALL = 543.00'), not just ambient spot elevations. The lack of explicit wall elevation labels means the requirement is not satisfied.
findings.explanation: Retaining walls with guardrails shown on Sheets 14-15 (likely >2 feet given guardrail requirement) do not show explicit top and bottom wall elevations.
findings.resolution: Add top and bottom elevation labels for all retaining walls greater than 2 feet in height, particularly the retaining walls with guardrails shown along the northern property boundary on Sheets 14 and 15.

findings.observation: Vision check on Sheet 14 confirmed that the retaining walls with guardrails are located on private property within the development site, inside the property line and adjacent to (but not within) the public sidewalk easements. Per the validation methodology, TCM 13.1.0 structural design criteria applies specifically to retaining walls 'in the right-of-way, easements, and any City property.' The methodology explicitly states to only flag this item for walls associated with roadway construction, ROW improvements, or easement areas, and notes that private development retaining walls are reviewed at building plan review.
findings.reasoning: While retaining walls >2 feet are proposed (walls with guardrails), they are located on private property, not in ROW, public easements, or City property. The validation methodology carves out private on-site retaining walls from completeness check review. Since these walls are not associated with roadway construction or located in ROW/easements/City property, the sealed structural drawing requirement does not apply at this completeness check stage.
findings.explanation: Retaining walls with guardrails are on private property, not in ROW, easements, or City property; private development walls reviewed at building plan stage per TCM 13.1.0.

findings.observation: Vision check on Sheet 15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 2 Of 2) found a labeled 'TRASH ROOM SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DETAILS' in the lower-middle section of Proposed Building 1, near the southern boundary. This indicates an interior trash collection location. No exterior dumpsters or garbage carts were found on the site plans reviewed.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires locations of existing and proposed dumpsters and garbage carts (interior or exterior) to be shown. The trash room label on Sheet 15 identifies the location of interior refuse collection, satisfying the requirement to show where garbage/trash will be collected. The reference to architectural plans for details is acceptable as the site plan establishes the location. Since this is new construction on a redevelopment site, no existing dumpsters/carts are expected.
findings.explanation: Trash room location shown on Sheet 15 within Proposed Building 1, identifying interior refuse collection location with reference to architectural plans for details.

findings.observation: Vision check on Sheet 14 confirmed proposed work adjacent to and encroaching into the ROW is identified and labeled. The plan shows proposed curb and gutter, planting zones, ADA ramps (Keynote 12), and curb inlets (Keynote 3) along Collier Street (labeled as 'COLLIER STREET (R.O.W. VARIES)'). Sheet 14 also shows a proposed variable width public sidewalk easement with associated improvements. The dimensional control plans clearly delineate ROW boundaries and show proposed improvements within or adjacent to those boundaries.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is to identify and label proposed work adjacent to or encroaching into the ROW. The plans show multiple ROW-related improvements along street frontages with labels identifying the work type (curb and gutter, ADA ramps, inlets, sidewalks, planting zones). The callouts and keynotes provide identification of the specific improvements. The relationship to ROW is clear through the ROW line delineations and street labels indicating 'R.O.W. VARIES.'
findings.explanation: ROW work identified and labeled on Sheet 14 including proposed curb and gutter, ADA ramps, curb inlets, and planting zones along Collier Street ROW.

summary: 9 of 11 items pass, 2 items fail, 0 items not-applicable. Failed items: existing ROW widths not dimensioned (CC-23-01) and retaining wall elevations not shown (CC-23-08). Items CC-23-05, CC-23-06, CC-23-07, and CC-23-09 are not applicable as no new roadway construction is proposed and retaining walls are on private property.
